battle.name: 巴達維起義
battle.brief: 公元69年五帝之年，下萊茵的巴達維協助軍倒戈，叛軍夜襲韋特拉營地、泅渡萊茵，最後被維佩蒂安自西班牙調來的軍團與工程兵封死在巴達維城。卡面羅馬重步兵象徵帝國真正的底子：兵源與補給線，最後取勝的不是甲胄，而是渡河權、圍城工事與糧秣。

kit.name: 羅馬重步兵
kit.history: 分段鎧甲配重盾。羅馬的戰力靠的是補充兵源與補給線，不是靠重裝。

countries: 巴達維起義是公元69年羅馬帝國五帝之年中發生在下萊茵的一次大規模叛亂，交戰雙方並非兩個國家，而是帝國核心與其邊疆的附庸體系。羅馬一方以維佩蒂安重新集中起來的中央軍為骨幹：公元69年駐在下萊茵的有第一密涅瓦、第十六高盧、第五雲雀、第二十二原初等軍團與多支協助軍，指揮權先後落在下萊茵總督霍爾德奧尼烏斯·弗拉庫斯，以及皇帝的兩位兄弟阿魯魯斯與普布利烏斯·維特里烏斯手中；公元70年，皇帝維佩蒂安自西班牙調來第一輔助、第二輔助等軍團，交由蘇爾皮基烏斯·加爾巴率領，凱里亞利斯接手前線圍城，最終在巴達維城（今日奈梅亨）完成平叛。叛軍一方以巴達維人為主，他們本是羅馬最尊貴的野蠻附庸，公元前一世紀以來以整建大隊的方式向帝國提供精銳步兵，同時在部落聯盟內享有免稅與自治的特權；從69年冬到70年，卡涅法特人、布魯克特里人、騰克特里人、通格里人與弗里西人相繼加入，70年初維佩蒂安在意大利取勝的消息傳到萊茵後，特里維里人與林戈內斯人也倒向叛軍，由因迪提奧馬魯斯率領，叛軍騎兵還兩度越過萊茵河掃蕩貝洛加（今比利時）一帶的高盧聚落。叛軍的訴求帶有明確的部落政治色彩：既然巴達維人替羅馬流血流血而其他日耳曼部落卻要照章交稅服役，那麼二者的差別不應存在；最終被羅馬平定的並非一個統一國家，而是一群各有算盤的部落聯盟。
countriesEn: The Batavian Revolt was a large-scale rising on the Lower Rhine in AD 69, in the middle of the Roman Empire's Year of the Five Emperors, and the two sides were not two states but the imperial core and the client system that surrounded it. The Roman side was built on the central army that Vespasian reconcentrated: the Lower Rhine garrison in 69 included the Legio I Minervia, XVI Gallica, V Alaudae and XXII Primigenia together with a number of auxiliary units, and command passed in turn to the Lower Rhine governor Hordeonius Flaccus and to the emperor's two brothers, Aulus and Publius Vitellius. In 70 the emperor Vespasian brought the Legio I Adiutrix and II Adiutrix over from Hispania, put the field army under Publius Sulpicius Galba, and left Cerialis to take over the siege operations that ended with the reduction of Batavia, modern Nijmegen. On the rebel side the Batavi stood in front: they had long been Rome's most privileged barbarian clients, furnishing picked infantry in complete cohorts to the empire since the first century BC and, in return, enjoying exemption from ordinary taxation and a measure of autonomy inside their tribal league. From the winter of 69 into 70 the Cannuveti, Bructeri, Tencteri, Tungri and Frisii joined in turn, and when news of Vespasian's victory in Italy reached the Rhine in 70 the Treveri and Lingones turned to the insurgents under Indutiomarus, while Batavian cavalry raided twice across the Rhine into Belgica, modern Belgium, dragging the Gallic communities of that region into the war. The movement carried an explicit tribal-political character: if the Batavi shed blood for Rome while other Germanic tribes paid tax and were conscripted, the difference between the two had no justification. What Rome finally put down was therefore not a single state but a loose coalition of tribes with separate interests.
people: 起義最關鍵的人物是加尤斯·尤利烏斯·奇維利斯。塔西佗描述他為巴達維出身、已在羅馬軍中效力約三十年的老兵，身材高大，滿面刀疤，能講一口流利的拉丁語，並曾因戰功獲得羅馬頒發的項鍊；起義爆發後，他被部眾推為首領，統率步兵與騎兵，夜襲韋特拉的羅馬軍營，並指揮後續越過萊茵河的襲擊。真正在政治層面代表部落利益的是他的族人克勞狄烏斯·奇維利斯：此人不通拉丁語，能以巴達維語發表不為羅馬意圖所左右的演說，負責把反對苛徵的主張傳遍各營。另一位重要人物是尤利烏斯·阿爾皮努斯，一位出身巴達維貴族騎士階層、曾兩度出使羅馬並與皇室往來的人物，他起初傾向與帝國談判，最後加入叛軍，與奇維利斯分工，負責與各部落首領協調並執行軍事計劃。羅馬方面的關鍵人物更多：公元69年下萊茵總督霍爾德奧尼烏斯·弗拉庫斯被自己麾下的士兵殺死，成為兵變失控的導火線；皇帝維特里烏斯由巴達維輔助軍抬上盾牌推舉為帝，卻在萊茵前線遭士兵以奇維利斯式的敬禮戲弄，聲望由此崩解，他本人於同年12月在羅馬被禁衛軍殺死，兩位兄弟普布利烏斯與阿魯魯斯在萊茵相繼兵變，或被部下所殺、或被處決。公元70年接手的維佩蒂安由其弟提圖斯與婿子圖密善輔佐，下令調兵，並在最後對巴達維人開出赦免條件，平叛的大軍由蘇爾皮基烏斯·加爾巴統籌，圍城與受降則由凱里亞利斯主持。特里維里人領袖因迪提奧馬魯斯在叛軍與皇帝之間反覆周旋，最終兵敗身死。
peopleEn: The key figure of the revolt was Gaius Julius Civilis. Tacitus describes him as a Batavian who had served about thirty years in the Roman army: a tall man with a face scarred by wounds, a fluent speaker of Latin who had once been awarded a military decoration at Rome. Once the revolt broke out he was acclaimed as leader by his own people, commanded the infantry and the horse, led the night attack on the Roman camp at Vetera, and directed the later raids across the Rhine. The man who spoke for the tribal interest in political terms was his kinsman Claudius Civilis: a man who did not know Latin, who delivered speeches in Batavian that no Roman interpreter could bend to Roman purposes, and who carried the demand for an end to the exactions from camp to camp. Another important figure was Julius Alpinus, a member of the Batavian equestrian order who had twice gone to Rome on embassies and kept up relations with the imperial household; he began by favouring negotiation and only at the end joined the insurgents, dividing the labour with Civilis by coordinating the tribal chiefs and carrying out the military plan. On the Roman side there were more names. The Lower Rhine governor Hordeonius Flaccus was killed by his own soldiers in 69, the spark that turned mutiny into open revolt. The emperor Vitellius was lifted on the shields of the Batavian auxiliaries and acclaimed, and then mocked on the Rhine by soldiers who greeted him with the so-called Civilis salute, which destroyed his credit; he himself was murdered by the Praetorian Guard at Rome in December of that year, while his two brothers Publius and Aulus mutinied in turn on the Rhine and were killed by their own men or executed. Vespasian, who took over in 70 with his brother Titus and his son-in-law Domitian, ordered the reinforcements and set the terms of the amnesty that the Batavians were finally offered; the field army was planned by Sulpicius Galba, while Cerialis directed the siege and the surrender. Indutiomarus, the Treveran leader, shifted back and forth between the rebels and the emperor and ended the war dead.
kits: 卡面這件羅馬重步兵（Legionary）象徵的是帝國的骨幹：公元前一世紀的標準形象是分段式金屬胸甲（lorica segmentata）配方曲面盾牌（scutum），配短劍（gladius）與重矛（pila）。但要老實說，公元69年這已是過時的標準：分段甲在行軍中被嫌沉重易壞，多數軍團與協助軍已改用鎖子甲（lorica hamata），盾牌也從方盾過渡到橢圓或圓角的大盾；卡面與本役現場大約相差一世紀。真正出現在萊茵的裝備包括：步兵的加長重矛、短劍與標槍，日耳曼式的框劍（framea，長身單刃直劍，在奈梅亨出土的巴達維騎兵墓葬中成組出現）、弓與複合反弓，騎兵專用的大盾與長刺槍（contus），以及標準營地器材：折疊盾板（scutum segmentum）、三角帳篷、工兵斧、鐵鍬與壕溝器材。攻城一側還有弩砲、投石與投擲槍，城防一側則是削尖木柵、填土牆與河堤缺口。輔助軍的遠射武器是羅馬式短弓與標槍，叛軍一側的日耳曼戰士則大量使用弓與投石索。運輸方面完全依賴萊茵河與瓦爾河：重型攻城器材與糧秣用平底貨船（navis oneraria）分批北運，軍隊行軍靠牛車與騾隊，馬匹既作騎乘也拉車，而公元70年末冬季的封河與結冰直接決定了圍城補給的節奏。
kitsEn: The Roman legionary on the card stands for the backbone of the empire: the standard image of the first century BC is a segmented metal cuirass (lorica segmentata) with a curved rectangular shield (scutum), a short sword (gladius) and a heavy spear (pila). It has to be said, though, that by AD 69 this was already an out-of-date standard. The segmented cuirass was disliked on the march for its weight and its habit of breaking, so most legions and auxiliaries had gone over to mail (lorica hamata), and shields were in transition from the rectangle to the oval or round-edged type; the card stands roughly a century away from the field of this war. The equipment actually present on the Rhine included the long heavy spear, the short sword and the javelin of the infantry, the Germanic framea with its long single-edged blade, known from the grouped burials of Batavian cavalrymen at Nijmegen, bows and composite bows, the large shield and long thrusting lance (contus) of the cavalry, and the standard camp kit: folding shield sections (scutum segmentum), the wedge tent, axes, spades and ditching tools. On the siege side there were ballistae, stone-throwers and throwing weapons, while the defence relied on sharpened stakes, earth walls and breaches opened in the river dyke. The ranged weapons of the auxiliaries were the short Roman bow and the javelin, while the Germanic warriors of the rebel side relied heavily on the bow and the sling. Transport depended wholly on the Rhine and the Waal: heavy siege material and provisions were moved northward in flat-bottomed cargo boats (navis oneraria) in batches, the armies marched with ox carts and mule trains, horses served both for riding and for draught, and the freezing and closing of the river in the late winter of 70 set the rhythm of the supply to the siege directly.
tactics: 叛軍全程避免與帝國主力正面決戰，走的是巴達維人最擅長的河與沼澤路線。公元69年秋，叛軍夜襲韋特拉（克桑滕）營區，用火把與長矛同時攻擊第一密涅瓦與第十六高盧兩個軍團的營壘，把營地、糧倉與武器庫一併燒毀；其後以騎兵為主的分隊兩度泅渡萊茵河，掃蕩貝洛加與上日耳曼，遇到羅馬主力便立即退入沼澤。奇維利斯還曾以舟船搭成浮橋，把部隊送到敵軍側翼，利用羅軍不熟當地水道的弱點。帝軍方面則嚴格照軍團條令辦事：宿營挖壕、築土壘、按圖設崗；圍城時在巴達維城外拉出環形封鎖線（circumvallation），在瓦爾河對岸另建營壘控制水路，再以投射兵器與工程兵封住島嶼唯一出入口，企圖餓斃守軍。公元70年末至71年初，叛軍企圖以突擊突破封鎖線，帝軍步軍縱隊在泥濘與壕溝之間接戰，叛軍因重裝與地形而失去速度，陣形一旦被切斷便無法重整，帝軍趁勢攻入城中。雙方的騎兵在追逐與包抄中扮演關鍵角色，尤其是巴達維騎兵，其裝備與戰技都勝過帝國的輔助騎兵。戰役的另一半是政治戰：維佩蒂安一面調兵圍剿，一面宣布赦免並允許巴達維人保留部落身份與兵役傳統，主張最力的首領與部眾在圍城後陸續放下武器，使叛軍失去繼續作戰的意志。
tacticsEn: The insurgents avoided pitched battle with the main Roman army throughout and fought along what the Batavians did best, the river and the marshes. In the autumn of 69 they struck the camps at Vetera, modern Xanten, by night, using torches and long spears at the same moment against the camps of the Legio I Minervia and XVI Gallica, burning the camp works, the granaries and the armoury together with them. Afterwards detachments led by the cavalry swam the Rhine twice, raiding Belgica and Germania Superior, and broke off into the marshes as soon as they met a Roman main force. Civilis also used boats lashed together as a floating bridge to place troops on the Roman flank, exploiting the fact that the Roman army was unfamiliar with the local waterways. The imperial side followed legionary discipline strictly: a ditch and an earthwork were dug around every camp, and the wall circuit of the blockade (circumvallation) was drawn around Batavia, with a second camp on the far bank of the Waal to control the water traffic, while artillery and engineers sealed the single approach to the island in the hope of starving the garrison. In the winter of 70 and the opening of 71 the rebels tried to break the blockade in a sortie, but the Roman maniples met them in the mud and between the ditches; the insurgents lost their speed in the heavy equipment and the broken ground, and once their line was cut they could not reform, which allowed the Roman infantry to carry the town. Cavalry played a decisive part in the pursuit and in the turning of the flanks, above all the Batavian horse, whose equipment and drill were better than those of the Roman auxiliary cavalry. Half of this war was political: while Vespasian moved troops against the insurgents he also proclaimed an amnesty and allowed the Batavians to keep their tribal identity and their tradition of service, and the chiefs and their followers came to lay down their arms one after another after the siege, taking the heart out of the rebel cause.
data: 有根據可寫的數字大致如下。普林尼《自然史》記載巴達維人向羅馬提供的兵員達三十五個大隊，這支部隊被視為帝國最精銳的協助軍之一。帝國一個軍團的標準員額約五千人，公元69年下萊茵至少駐有第一密涅瓦、第十六高盧、第五雲雀、第二十二原初四個軍團，連同協助軍與騎兵，駐軍總量在兩萬人上下；公元70年平叛時，自西班牙調來的第一輔助與第二輔助等軍團再行加入，圍城階段帝軍投入的兵力達數萬人量級。叛軍方面，塔西佗沒有留下精確總數，但從數支巴達維大隊加上卡涅法特、布魯克特里、騰克特里等部落人數推估，起義兵力同樣是數萬人量級，其中巴達維騎兵數量在數百至數千之間。地點與距離：巴達維城（奈梅亨）位於瓦爾河中的島上，距韋特拉營地沿河約六十至七十公里，距波恩約一百公里，羅馬軍徒步行軍每日約二十至二十五公里，師旅調動以週計。時間：公元69年初兵變起，69年10月攻破韋特拉營壘，70年末至71年初巴達維城被攻破並受降，全過程約一年半到兩年。傷亡方面，兩份主要史料都只留下概括描述，叛軍首謀者被處決，餘部未遭大規模屠殺；奇維利斯退入沼澤後身亡，屍體由部眾找到並安葬。
dataEn: The figures that can be given on good authority are roughly these. Pliny the Elder records that the Batavi furnished the Roman army with thirty-five cohorts, a body regarded as one of the finest auxiliary forces in the empire. A Roman legion normally numbered about five thousand men, and at least four legions stood on the Lower Rhine in 69, the I Minervia, XVI Gallica, V Alaudae and XXII Primigenia, with auxiliaries and cavalry bringing the garrison total to something like twenty thousand; when the revolt was suppressed in 70 the Legio I Adiutrix and II Adiutrix came over from Hispania as well, bringing the Roman force committed to the siege up to tens of thousands. On the rebel side Tacitus leaves no exact figure, but from several Batavian cohorts together with the Cannuveti, Bructeri and Tencteri the insurgents can likewise be reckoned in the tens of thousands, among them a Batavian horse numbering in the hundreds or thousands. Place and distance: Batavia, modern Nijmegen, lay on an island in the Waal, about sixty to seventy kilometres along the river from the camp at Vetera and about a hundred kilometres from Bonn, and a Roman column on foot covered some twenty to twenty-five kilometres a day, so that the movement of the armies was measured in weeks. Time: the mutiny began early in 69, Vetera was overrun in October 69, Batavia was taken and surrendered in the late winter of 70 and the opening of 71, and the whole business took roughly a year and a half to two years. Casualties are given only in general terms by both principal sources; the leaders of the revolt were executed, the rank and file were not massacred, and Civilis died after hiding in the marshes, his body being found and buried by his own people.
cause: 起義的根子埋在一個不平等的制度裡。巴達維部族自公元前一世紀以來是羅馬的附庸王國，以整建大隊的形式提供兵員，作為回報免於常稅並保有自治；與他們相鄰的卡涅法特人、特里維里人、騰克特里人等卻要照章交稅、照章徵召常備兵，於是同一條萊茵河兩側出現了為何他們能豁免、我們卻要的不平。公元69年的政治崩潰把這個積怨推上檯面：加爾巴、奧托、維特里烏斯在半年內相繼被軍隊推舉，萊茵指揮系統不斷換人，兵員被抽往意大利，前線只剩輔助軍撐著，而輔助軍素來被視為可以消耗的次等兵力。公元60至69年間羅馬在萊茵的戰事裡，巴達維人是最前線的打手，卻常被扣下戰利品。最後的導火線是維佩蒂安上台後的處置：解除巴達維大隊的武裝、取消他們的獨立旗號與編制，把人調往不列顛或拆散混編，這等於否認巴達維人用血換來的地位。奇維利斯與阿爾皮努斯這些已經羅馬化的巴達維精英，本來就自認比高盧行省居民高貴得多，卻發現自己只是皇帝眼中一支可以解散的野蠻部隊；起義於是他們把部落尊嚴與帝國的政治危機接在一起點燃。
causeEn: The roots of the revolt lay in an unequal system. Since the first century BC the Batavian tribe had been a client kingdom of Rome, furnishing troops in complete cohorts and receiving in return exemption from the ordinary tribute and a measure of autonomy; its neighbours, the Cannuveti, the Treveri and the Tencteri, paid tax and were conscripted into the regular forces, and so along a single stretch of the Rhine there arose the question of why one people was exempt and the others were not. The political collapse of 69 brought that grievance to the surface: Galba, Otho and Vitellius were each acclaimed by the troops within half a year, the command on the Rhine was repeatedly reshuffled, the manpower was drained away to Italy, and the front was left in the hands of the auxiliaries, who were always treated as the expendable second-line troops. In the campaigns on the Rhine between 60 and 69 the Batavi had done the hardest work at the front and were often denied their share of the spoils. The last spark was the disposition Vespasian made after he came to the throne: disarming the Batavian cohorts, cancelling their own standards and their separate organisation, and transferring the men to Britain or breaking them up in the line. That was in effect a denial of everything the Batavians had bought with blood. Civilis and Alpinus, Batavians Romanised to the bone, had always considered themselves far above the inhabitants of the Gallic provinces, and now found they were only a barbarian unit the emperor could dissolve; and so they joined tribal pride to the imperial crisis and lit the fuse.
impact: 巴達維起義是公元一世紀西部行省最後一次大規模的部落起義，它改變的不只是萊茵的防線。巴達維作為羅馬附庸王國的自治地位就此終結，尼梅亨從部落首邑變成下日耳曼行省的軍鎮與行政中心，羅馬從此直接管理這片三角洲地帶，過去那種以忠誠的野蠻人換取自治的歐洲式治理模式在西部收場。巴達維人本身則以另一種方式延續：維佩蒂安赦免了他們，允許他們保留部落身份、返回家園、繼續為帝國提供兵員，隨後大批巴達維人隨軍前往不列顛，第九巴達維大隊等部隊駐紮哈德良長城一線，作為帝國北方防線的重要骨幹，其作風一直延續到二世紀以後。在軍制上，這場叛亂也把羅馬輔助軍的樣板固定下來：曲盾、短劍與日耳曼長劍並用的裝備組合、整建大隊的編制，以及以整族為單位的徵募方式，經此役之後成為帝國邊軍的常態，禁衛軍中以日耳曼人為主的近衛大隊沿用的也是這一路數。政治上，萊茵的失控直接削弱了維特里烏斯：他的主力與補給被叛軍切斷在北方，意大利戰線上的勝負因此更快決定，也迫使維佩蒂安必須先鞏固萊茵再處理其他戰線，五帝之年的西部最終不是被另一場內戰收場，而是被一場鎮壓與赦免並用的邊疆叛亂收場。維佩蒂安的寬大同時成為帝國的樣板與對照：公元70年代特里維里人、卡馬西人接連起事時，鎮壓就明顯更嚴厲，政策的兩面性在十年之間就看得出來。
impactEn: The Batavian Revolt was the last great tribal rising in the western provinces of the first century AD, and it changed more than the Rhine line. The autonomous position of the Batavi as a Roman client kingdom came to an end: Nijmegen, formerly the tribal capital, became a garrison town and administrative centre of the province of Germania Inferior, and Rome from then on governed the delta directly, closing the chapter of that Gallic-style arrangement in which autonomy was bought with loyalty. The Batavi themselves went on in a different form. Vespasian pardoned them, allowed them to keep their tribal identity, to go home and to go on providing troops to the empire, and large numbers of them were afterwards carried to Britain with the armies, where units such as the Cohors IX Batavorum took station along Hadrian's Wall and remained the backbone of the northern frontier into the second century. Militarily the revolt also fixed the pattern of the Roman auxiliary: the combination of the curved shield, the short sword and the Germanic long sword, the organisation in complete cohorts and the recruiting of whole peoples by name became the standing practice of the frontier army after this war, and the Germanic bodyguard cohorts of the Praetorian Guard followed the same line. Politically the collapse on the Rhine cut Vitellius off at the root: his troops and his supplies were severed in the north, the Italian war was decided faster for that reason, and Vespasian was forced to secure the Rhine before he could deal with his other fronts, so that the west of the empire in the Year of the Five Emperors was closed not by a second civil war but by a frontier rebellion put down with a mixture of severity and pardon. Vespasian's clemency became at once a model and a foil: when the Treveri and the Camasi rose in the seventies the suppression was markedly harsher, and the two faces of the policy were visible within ten years.
result: 平叛的結局是公元70年末至71年初的巴達維城。帝軍攻破環形封鎖後，叛軍在城中與城郊反覆抵抗，突圍行動在泥濘與封鎖線之間被打散，首領奇維利斯退入沼澤身亡，屍體後來被找到，由部眾自行安葬；克勞狄烏斯·奇維利斯與阿爾皮努斯等主張最力者被清算，族內其餘的人則被判處解散大隊。帝軍沒有屠城，這一點是這場戰役最被記住的部分：維佩蒂安宣布赦免，允許巴達維人保留部落建制、返回家園，並繼續保有向帝國提供兵員的傳統，條件是繳械、交付人質並解散起義期間自行編成的部隊。善後上，羅馬重整了下萊茵的駐軍配置，把部分協助軍與巴達維分隊調往不列顛，重建營壘，恢復瓦爾河與萊茵河的航運與渡口控制，萊茵邊界回到可控狀態。從戰術角度看，這場戰爭的勝負手不在會戰，而在三件事：河流的渡用權、島嶼要塞的封鎖工程，以及糧秣能否靠水運持續供給；巴達維人靠民族動員一度把帝國拉下戰馬，卻輸在攻城技術與後勤耐力，最後靠皇帝開出的赦免條件收場。塔西佗記下了受降的過程與帝國的寬大處置：勝利者沒有屠殺，敗者交出人質，這成了這場叛亂在後世被記住的方式。
resultEn: The business was settled at Batavia in the late winter of 70 and the opening of 71. After the blockade was broken the rebels fought back in and around the town, their sortie was scattered in the mud and against the line, and their leader Civilis withdrew into the marshes and died there; his body was found later and buried by his own people, while Claudius Civilis and Alpinus, the men who had argued hardest for the revolt, were liquidated, and the rest of the tribe was sentenced to have its cohorts disbanded. The Roman army did not sack the town, and that is the part of this war that history remembered. Vespasian proclaimed an amnesty, allowed the Batavians to keep their tribal organisation, to go home and to go on providing troops to the empire, on condition that they gave up their arms, handed over hostages and dissolved the units they had raised on their own during the revolt. In the aftermath Rome reorganised the Lower Rhine garrison, moved part of the auxiliaries and the Batavian detachments to Britain, rebuilt the camp works and regained control of the navigation and the crossings of the Waal and the Rhine, and the frontier returned to a manageable state. Tactically the outcome turned on three things rather than on any pitched battle: who could use the river, the engineering of the blockade of the island fortress, and whether food could be supplied continuously by water. The Batavians used their tribal mobilisation to pull the empire off its balance for a time, but they lost on siegecraft and on endurance of supply, and the war ended on the terms the emperor offered. Tacitus records the process of the surrender and the moderation with which Rome handled it: the victors did not kill, the defeated gave hostages, and that is how this revolt came to be remembered.
